{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nm-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"ae7bc582ed50fa0dbaeae03bed94964526795e26947e6d8c82068eadf2a4c727","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nm-class-std:lineage:44","source_registry_sha256":"22599efcb4852b796972acef6eb09f4cfe8d16ca15887f7ea7660c7748b4df92","source_liveness_sha256":"6766993f61347d495f390e08c7d8b1c44de597b6249cdb10686ea7f9f38e1ea3"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning","heading":"C2 — Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A03
Before turning left across approaching traffic, wait for a gap large enough to complete the movement safely. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A03
Before turning left, check the destination street for vehicles or pedestrians that could leave you stranded in the opposing traffic path. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A03
Immediately before turning left across oncoming traffic, look once more toward the oncoming vehicles. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A03
Before turning right, check for vehicles approaching from your left. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A03
Before turning right, check whether an oncoming vehicle will turn left into your path. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A03
Check for pedestrians in the destination crossing before beginning a right turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A03
A posted prohibition overrides the handbook’s permission to turn right on red. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A03
The handbook permits a left turn from a one-way street into another one-way street unless the turn is prohibited. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A03
Do not assume a traffic sign or signal guarantees that cross traffic will stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A03
Look left and right at an intersection even when crossing traffic faces a red light or a stop sign. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R11 | anchor: A03
Use particular care just after a light turns green because cross traffic may still try to hurry through. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R12 | anchor: A03
If your cross-street view is blocked after stopping, creep forward slowly until approaching traffic becomes visible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R13 | anchor: A03
Moving forward slowly can let crossing drivers notice the vehicle’s front and give them a chance to slow or warn you. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R14 | anchor: A03
Scan the roadside carefully near shops, parking lots, road work, busy sidewalks, playgrounds and schoolyards because people may enter the road there. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R15 | anchor: A03
At every railroad approach, reduce speed and look both ways along the tracks for a train. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R16 | anchor: A03
A crossing where you have never seen a train must still be checked for an approaching train. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R17 | anchor: A03
Cross tracks only when enough room exists beyond them to hold the vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R18 | anchor: A03
At a multitrack crossing, let a passing train move well away before crossing because it can hide another train. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R19 | anchor: A03
Monitor rear traffic more frequently when the traffic stream is heavy. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R20 | anchor: A03
Rear checks reveal a following vehicle that is too close or approaching too quickly. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R21 | anchor: A03
Rear-traffic checks are especially important before a lane change, slowdown, backing movement or descent of a long or steep hill. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R22 | anchor: A03
Before changing lanes, check both the side and the rear for vehicles in the intended lane. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R23 | anchor: A03
Lane changing includes merging from an entrance ramp and entering traffic from a curb or shoulder. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R24 | anchor: A03
Use both rearview and side mirrors to check whether the target lane is clear. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R25 | anchor: A03
Before changing lanes, make sure another vehicle is not about to pass you. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R26 | anchor: A04
Before moving sideways, look over your shoulder toward that direction to check near the vehicle’s rear corners. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R27 | anchor: A04
The rear-corner areas invisible through the mirrors are blind spots. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R28 | anchor: A04
Side and rear checks should be brief because traffic ahead can stop unexpectedly while you look away. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R29 | anchor: A04
Use mirrors while preparing to merge, change lanes or enter the road so you can continue monitoring ahead. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R30 | anchor: A04
Check over your shoulder for blind-spot traffic immediately before changing lanes. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R31 | anchor: A04
Several quick looks are preferable to one long look away from the road ahead. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R32 | anchor: A04
During a lane change, track both the traffic ahead and the traffic in the lane you are entering. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R33 | anchor: A04
If there is a lane beyond the one you plan to enter, check it for another driver moving into the same space. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R34 | anchor: A04
Motorcyclists, bicyclists and pedestrians can be harder to notice than cars or trucks. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R35 | anchor: A04
Be particularly alert for other road users when pulling into the roadway from a curb or driveway. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R36 | anchor: A04
Check rear traffic whenever you slow, especially for a sudden slowdown or a stop at an unexpected driveway or parking space. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R37 | anchor: A04
Keep backing movements to a minimum because the area behind a vehicle is difficult to see. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R38 | anchor: A04
A parking space that lets you drive through can allow a forward departure instead of backing out. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R39 | anchor: A04
Before entering the vehicle to back it, check behind for children or low objects hidden from the driver’s seat. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R40 | anchor: A04
When backing, the handbook describes resting the right arm on the seatback and turning to look through the rear window. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R41 | anchor: A04
Do not rely only on the mirrors while backing because they do not show the area directly behind the vehicle. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R42 | anchor: A04
Reverse slowly because controlling the steering is harder while moving backward. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R43 | anchor: A04
Use a person outside to help guide a backing movement whenever possible. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R44 | anchor: A04
During a long or steep descent, watch the mirrors for vehicles gaining speed behind you. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R45 | anchor: A04
On downhill grades, stay alert for large trucks or buses approaching too fast. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]
